bindings.label: Patient has painful oral erosions that began 2 years before
Patient is a White man in his 50s with medical history of recurrent respiratory infections and diarrhea; previous intestinal biopsy showed unspecific findings and absence of apoptosis.
Patient reported a 5-kg weight loss attributed to impaired intake due to oral lesions.
Mediastinal mass was detected during chest radiography performed for pneumonia.
Physical examination revealed whitish edematous lacy patches with erosions on the dorsal and lateral aspects of the tongue and buccal mucosa; skin and nails were not involved.
Lingual biopsy shows lichenoid interface inflammation with fibrinogen deposition and negative DIF/IIF
Laboratory tests show decreased IgG, reduced B cells, and inverted CD4:CD8 ratio
Mediastinal mass is confirmed as type AB thymoma
All three expert analyses confirm Good syndrome based on type AB thymoma and immunodeficiency laboratory findings
